label: Cuban Collar
note: Owner-uploaded reference images. Authoritative for construction/appearance; NOT usable as the tech-pack illustration (not line art, or shows multiple options).

references.evidence: Colour photo of a man in a white linen camp shirt, cropped chin-to-thigh. The collar is a wide flat lapel-style fold lying against the shirt front, notched where the fold meets the front edge, with no separate collar band and no throat button/buttonhole - the neckline sits open in a shallow V. Front placket buttons start below the collar break. Two flapped chest patch pockets and long sleeves also visible.
references.ownerNotes: the collar should fade back a 1/3 of the way back. collar fold shouldn't go all the way around follow style in illustration

references.evidence: Colour lifestyle photo, man in a taupe knit shirt against a plaster wall. Collar is a single flat revere/camp fold with a clear notch, laid open against the chest, no collar band and no fastening at the throat; the neckline is an open V down to the first fastened front button. Five front buttons visible down the placket.
references.ownerNotes: the collar should fade back a 1/3 of the way back. collar fold shouldn't go all the way around follow style in illustration

references.evidence: Tight colour photo cropped to the neck/chest of a cream textured shirt. The camp collar is the subject: a wide flat fold lying directly on the chest, a distinct notch where the fold breaks at the front edge, the fold visibly running out toward the shoulder rather than encircling the neck, bare neck above it with no band and no throat button. Two front buttons visible below the collar break; edge-stitched collar and placket edges readable.
